I liked it, although I should probably adjust my voting rubric for this series so that "well-written and engaging" isn't the sole criteria for an upvote.

The Navarro stuff didn't mean much to me, and most read like the "remember Budapest?" stuff in Avengers. I get that this was released sort-of in tandem with Alphabet stuff, but without a day-by-day calendar of when stuff was released four years ago, the only real option is to plough through one canon, then another, then another, or else be bogged down in a swamp of crosslinks. Not a critique, more an observation with the benefit of hindsight.

So far as criticisms go, the bit between Jason and Medea being captured and Anderson showing for murder would've probably benefited from some short intermediary piece. As it is, it feels a bit like it jumps from A to C. Additionally, I wasn't really vibing with the jumping perspectives; I get that it was anchored by "stuff Phineas set up," but it still felt disjointed.

Finally, I'm not sure what the deal is with Anderson declaring that he's going to restore the equilibrium to his relationship with Phineas when he's the one who disturbed it, but the author's definitely earned a measure of trust, so I'mma just roll with it.

item.title: Author Post
item.content:encoded:
It is time for another Anderson Robotics tale, methinks. This time with yet more Navarro, Merlo, and all the other characters you have come to know and love.

Special thanks to TwistedGears, TyGently, Randomini, ProcyonLotor, and Taffeta for their feedback and help developing this new installment.

There will be one more installment in this series that I have come to call “Austringers.” So stay tuned for the inevitable robo-wizard battles that are to follow in the finale.

Additionally, those of you wondering about the title, I took it from a Chess glossary.

Consolidation:
The improvement of a player's position by the reposition of one or more pieces to better square(s), typically after a player's attack or combination has left his or her pieces in poor positions or uncoordinated.

I felt it was fitting.

Enjoy the tale.

Edit: Additionally, if you have yet to read the other tales in this series: Ties That Bind and Realignment, I would highly recommend it.
